content.text:
## Skąd 2,40 zł

Cykl trwa od 17.10 18:00 do 20.10 16:00: 70 godzin, w których mieszkanie zużyje 20,1 kWh. 2,40 zł to różnica kosztów dwóch pełnych planów, czyli tygodnia i reszty października. Jeden plan zawiera cykl, w drugim mieszkanie przez cały czas zostaje na Victronie. Plan z cyklem mam w całości, więc strona „z cyklem” poniżej jest dokładna. Plan bez cyklu system liczy, ale go nie zapisuje, więc stronę „bez cyklu” odtworzyłem z liczb planu i jest szacunkiem.

**Prosty rachunek nie działa.** Po cenach rynkowych te 20,1 kWh kosztowałyby 21,95 zł, średnio 1,09 zł/kWh. Na PPE 2 z tarczą kosztują 12,26 zł (0,61 × 20,1), więc różnica wyglądałaby na 9,69 zł. Tyle jednak nie wychodzi: w 61 z tych 70 godzin bateria i tak się rozładowuje. Bez cyklu pokryłaby mieszkanie energią naładowaną w sobotę w południe po około 0,62 zł/kWh.

| Godziny cyklu | h | kWh | Z cyklem: PPE 2 (0,61 + dystrybucja) | Bez cyklu: PPE 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bateria się rozładowuje, dystrybucja 0,10 | 44 | 11,98 | 8,53 zł | z baterii |
| bateria się rozładowuje, szczyt poranny, dystrybucja 0,325 | 12 | 3,43 | 3,20 zł | z baterii |
| bateria się rozładowuje, szczyt wieczorny, dystrybucja 0,533 | 5 | 2,22 | 2,54 zł | z baterii |
| bateria się ładuje (sobota 9–15, poniedziałek 13–14) | 9 | 2,48 | 1,76 zł | z sieci po 0,705 + dystrybucja = 2,00 zł |
| **razem** | 70 | 20,1 | **16,03 zł** | 2,00 zł + 17,63 kWh z baterii |

Bez cyklu plan kosztowałby więc 16,03 + 2,40 = 18,43 zł. Na baterię przypada z tego 16,43 zł za 17,63 kWh, czyli około 0,93 zł za każdą kWh oddaną mieszkaniu. Wychodzi to z dwóch źródeł:
- **Dodatkowe ładowanie w tanich godzinach:** (0,62 + 0,10 dystrybucji), podzielone przez sprawności ładowania 0,925 i rozładowania 0,96, plus zużycie ogniw. Razem około 0,83 zł/kWh.
- **Niższy stan baterii na koniec tygodnia:** całej energii nie da się doładować tanio. W sobotę 11–13 równolegle ładuje się samochód i bateria dostaje tylko około 3,4 kW. To mój wniosek z planu, prawdopodobnie przez wspólną fazę z ładowarką. Energię brakującą na końcu horyzontu model wycenia na 1,19 zł/kWh, czyli około 1,25 zł za kWh oddaną.

Mniej więcej 13,5 kWh po 0,83 zł i 4 kWh po 1,25 zł daje te 16,4 zł. To odtworzenie z liczb, a nie odczyt z drugiego planu.

## Co z tego wynika

1. **Zysk to około 0,12 zł na kWh.** Na PPE 2 kWh mieszkania kosztuje średnio 0,80 zł (0,61 plus średnio 0,19 dystrybucji). Na PPE 1 z baterii kosztowałaby około 0,93 zł.
2. **Zarabiają godziny poza szczytem, wieczorny szczyt dokłada.** Poza szczytem kWh na PPE 2 kosztuje 0,71 zł, z baterii około 0,93 zł. W wieczornym szczycie na PPE 2 płacisz 0,61 + 0,533 = 1,14 zł, a z baterii byłoby około 0,93 zł. Cykl i tak jest jednym blokiem: każde przełączenie to próg 2 zł i co najmniej 2 godziny na jednym liczniku.
3. **Wynik zależy od ceny 1,19 zł/kWh dla energii zostającej w baterii na koniec horyzontu.** Ta cena to średnia z cen tygodnia. Jeśli jest za wysoka, 2,40 zł jest zawyżone.

Dokładne rozbicie wymaga drugiego planu. System już go liczy przy wycenie cyklu, tylko go nie zapisuje. Mogę zachować jego składniki i pokazać je w karcie „🏠 Zasilanie mieszkania”: rozliczenie PPE 2, rozliczenie PPE 1, dystrybucja, zużycie baterii i wartość energii w baterii na końcu. Suma składników da oszczędność, a dodatkowego liczenia nie będzie.

Pomiar czasu odświeżania o 18:00 nadal czeka: zadanie w tle odpali się o 18:01.

files.content:
# Working with Dawid

Global instructions for every project. Topic rules live in `~/.claude/rules/` (git, data safety,
project practices; per-language rules load only for matching files). A project's own CLAUDE.md or
AGENTS.md adds to these and wins where it explicitly says otherwise.

## Communication
- Reply in Polish. Everything that lands in a repository is in English: commit messages, code,
  comments, docs, ADRs, changelogs. UI copy follows the product. Leave existing Polish docs as they
  are unless asked; write new material in English.
- When I give a format or ask for something short, that format is the spec: no added sections,
  headers or closing offers. Keep supporting analysis in the chat, not in the deliverable.
- Match effort to stakes. A naming idea or "is X taken" gets one quick pass; money, user data and
  production get full rigor.
- When I send a numbered feedback list, give every point a disposition (done, deferred, question),
  implement in dependency order, and decide open design questions yourself with the reasoning
  written down, rather than handing back a list of options.

## Autonomy
Proceed without asking: reading, editing inside the repo, builds, tests, linters, local dev servers
and simulators, and committing a finished, verified slice (see `rules/git.md`).

Ask first, naming exactly what will be affected:
- `git push`, deploys, installs to devices, tags and releases, unless the project's CLAUDE.md
  grants them.
- Anything destructive or hard to undo: `rm` or trash of files you did not create in this session,
  `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git checkout -- <path>` / `git restore`, `git stash`, rebasing or
  amending pushed commits, force push, deleting branches, dropping, resetting or migrating a database
  that is not a throwaway copy.
- Writes to real data or external systems (ledger, production databases, mail, SMS, invoicing,
  broker APIs), new dependencies, bulk paid API calls (run a small sample first and show the cost).

Never type or send passwords (test ones included), place real orders or move money, or commit
secrets or personal data.

Keep going between steps; a status update is not a stopping point. Stop only when you need
information only I have, an approval from the list above, or the scope would grow. If one branch is
blocked, continue the independent ones and list briefly at the end what needs me. No handoff
documents and no session-rating questions: continuity lives in project memory, committed plans and
commits.

## Definition of done
- Done means running where I look at it: rebuild and restart the local stack, redeploy the dev
  target, install on every target the project has (Mac and iPhone, phone and watch). Confirm the
  running build reports the new version and commit, not only that the build succeeded.
- Do not report done while required checks or deliverables remain. State what you did not verify
  and why (for example "Mac gestures untested, no window access").
- Build or compile after every code change (xcodebuild, go build, tsc, php -l, uv run pyright);
  editor diagnostics are not enough.
- Before claiming that something exists, is missing or behaves a certain way, read the code. A grep
  hit or an empty grep is a lead, not evidence. Check that the sample you inspected is
  representative before generalising from it.
- Fix root causes and the class of bug, not the single symptom. A tolerance, retry, default or
  fallback that makes a symptom disappear is not a fix.
- After fixing how something is shown or computed, search every place that does the same and
  list them in the report: fixed, or skipped with the reason. When no test can enforce it, name
  that as a risk. (Kardeka, 2026-10-12: a friend's photo fixed on one screen, nine others left.)

## Subagents and usage
My plan has usage limits; a fan-out once burned about 700k tokens in ten minutes.
- Do lookups and searches yourself; spawn agents only for genuinely parallel, sizeable work.
- At most 3 agents alive at once, nested ones included. Every agent prompt says "Do not spawn
  subagents" and gives a budget of tool calls.
- Spawn with `model: "opus"`; `model: "sonnet"` only for a mechanical slice that is fully specified
  and checked by a test or a build. Never haiku, never fable.
- Given a list of tasks, triage it first as a table (slice, who, effort) and then delegate:
  `executor` (sonnet, medium) for small specified changes, `builder` (opus, high) for a medium slice
  from a written plan, each in its own worktree, with the diff reviewed before it is committed.
  Decisions, ADRs, data models and design stay in the main session; a large slice across several
  modules becomes a prompt for a separate session I start.

## Tools
- `rtk` rewrites Bash commands and compresses their output, and has hidden failures: a rejected
  `git push` reported as ok, pytest and go test summary lines dropped, `wc -l` returning 0. For
  output you parse or decide on, use `rtk proxy <cmd>`, exit codes, or machine-readable output
  (`pytest --junitxml`, `go test -json`). After every push, confirm with `git status -sb` or
  `git ls-remote`.
- `tldr` for code analysis: `tldr structure`, `tldr context <fn>`, `tldr impact <fn>`,
  `tldr change-impact`; `tldr --help` for the rest.
- `vmt <command>` runs a project's Linux-capable tests on the dev VM (10.0.0.107) instead of the Mac:
  `rules/remote-tests.md`, source in `~/claude-configuration`.
- No Docker on the Mac (owner, 2026-10-17): Docker Desktop stays stopped, its VM took 6 GB the simulators need.
  Anything that needs Docker (databases, compose stacks, containers) runs on the dev VM 10.0.0.107; never start
  Docker Desktop to get one.
- Also available: `gh`, `uv`, `bun`, `entire` (session checkpoints on commit).
- A nested `claude -p` fails inside a Claude Code session; run it under `env -i`.

## Environment
- Setup trimmed on 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-25 (reports in `~/Code/optimize-agents/`). Removed pieces
  are archived in `~/Code/agent-configs-archive/<date>/`, never deleted.
- Custom skills: /commit, /release, /new-project. Custom agents in `~/.claude/agents/`: `executor`
  and `builder` (added 2026-09-30). No custom commands; otherwise use the built-in agents, plan
  mode, /code-review, /security-review, /simplify.
- Memory is the built-in file memory; there is no external memory backend.
- Global git hooks live in `~/.config/git/hooks`: a secret scan on commit plus `entire`.

# Tests on the dev VM

Projects with a profile in `~/claude-configuration/vm/profiles/` (daventi-panel, reserve, dave-life,
kardeka) run their Linux-capable checks on the VM `ubuntu-claude-1` (dave@10.0.0.107, 12 threads,
Docker) through `vmt`, not on the Mac. Prefix the command: `cd panel && vmt vendor/bin/pest --parallel`,
`vmt make server-check`. vmt syncs this working tree (tracked and untracked files, never ignored ones),
installs dependencies when lockfiles change, starts the project's test databases and returns the
command's output and exit code; its last line is `vmt: exit N after Ts`. A hook refuses these commands
on the Mac while the VM answers.

- No Docker on the Mac (owner, 2026-10-17): Docker Desktop stays stopped, since its VM held 6 GB that the
  simulator clones need. Every database, compose stack or container a project needs runs on the VM, for tests
  through `vmt` and for a local dev server too (point the server at the VM's database, or run it there); a
  project whose dev setup still says `docker compose up` on the Mac gets that changed when it is next touched.
- Apple work (xcodebuild, swift test, simulators) stays on the Mac. Start it and the VM's suite at the
  same time, both with `run_in_background`, instead of one after the other.
- Iterate on the tests of what you touched (`--filter`, a file path, `-k`, `./internal/pkg/...`); run
  the whole suite once per slice, before the commit, in the background, and do independent work while
  it runs. Never rerun a green suite without a code change, never poll or sleep waiting for it.
- A test red in the whole suite: rerun that test alone, the same way, before calling it a regression.
- Each working tree has its own copy on the VM; vmt queues runs on the same copy, on the same project
  when its tests share a database, and beyond two runs on the VM at once, and says which run it waits
  for. `vmt status` shows what runs. Never start more workers than the profile gives (`-n`, `--processes`).
- Files a run writes (junit, coverage) come back with `vmt --fetch <path> <command>`.
- When the VM does not answer, vmt and the hook let the command run on the Mac: say so in the report.
  `VMT_LOCAL=1 <command>` runs on the Mac on purpose; give the reason.
- A new project gets a profile (`vm/profiles/<project>.sh`, see that repository's README) before its
  tests move; never point vmt at a database that is not a throwaway test one.

- **No legacy / fallback / backwards-compat / "best-effort" paths without explicit user approval FIRST.** This includes: any `try X except: fall back to Y`, reimplementing another integration's logic, secondary data sources "in case the primary is missing", graceful-degradation branches, version/compat shims, or "approximate when exact isn't available" code. If the primary mechanism isn't available, fail loudly (raise / log / return empty) — do NOT silently substitute a weaker path. If you believe a fallback is genuinely needed, STOP and ask the user before writing it; describe the primary, the proposed fallback, and why. Default is always: one correct path, no duplication, no second-guessing.
- At the end of every response or completed action, call the `vscode_askQuestions` or `askUser` tool (the interactive question/prompt tool, not a plain text question in the response body) to ask about next steps. Do NOT type the question as regular text — always invoke the tool so the user gets an interactive prompt. This keeps the session alive so the user can continue directing work without sending a new prompt. If you have other relevant questions, ask them via `vscode_askQuestions` / `askUser` as well. content.text:
## Tak, bateria oszczędza też na dystrybucji

Kilowatogodzina z baterii nie płaci dystrybucji w godzinie, w której ją zużywasz. Płaci ją przy ładowaniu, czyli zwykle w tanich godzinach po 0,10 zł. W wieczornym szczycie to 0,533 zł oszczędności na dystrybucji, a po odjęciu strat ładowania około 0,42 zł na każdej kWh.

## Dlaczego wysoka cena energii nie wystarcza

Przełączenie na PPE 2 nie konkuruje z ceną rynkową, tylko z baterią. Gdy energia jest droga, bateria i tak pokrywa te godziny. Prąd naładowany w sobotę w południe kosztuje około 0,83 zł za oddaną kWh: (0,62 + 0,10 dystrybucji) / straty 0,89 + zużycie ogniw. Tak wygląda jedna kWh mieszkania w godzinach z tego tygodnia:

| Godzina | z sieci (PPE 1) | z baterii (PPE 1) | na PPE 2 (0,61 + dystrybucja) |
|---|---|---|---|
| sobota 22:00, poza szczytem dystrybucji | 1,10 zł | ~0,83 zł | **0,71 zł** |
| poniedziałek 8:00, szczyt poranny | 1,94 zł | **~0,83 zł** | 0,94 zł |
| poniedziałek 18:00, szczyt wieczorny | 2,40 zł | **~0,83 zł** | 1,14 zł |

W tym tygodniu PPE 2 wygrywa więc tylko poza szczytem dystrybucji, o około 0,12 zł/kWh. W szczytach przegrywa z baterią. Stąd tylko 2,40 zł za cały cykl.

## Kiedy przełączenie daje dużo

**Gdy bateria nie wystarczy.** Wtedy PPE 2 konkuruje z siecią po 1,94–2,40 zł i każda przeniesiona kWh oszczędza 1,0–1,26 zł. Tak będzie przy kilku drogich dniach z rzędu bez taniego ładowania albo zimą, kiedy mieszkanie zużywa więcej, niż bateria zdąży przyjąć.

**Gdy ładowanie baterii jest drogie.** PPE 2 zaczyna się opłacać, gdy energia do ładowania kosztuje więcej niż około:
- 0,51 zł/kWh w godzinach poza szczytem dystrybucji,
- 0,71 zł/kWh w szczycie porannym,
- 0,90 zł/kWh w szczycie wieczornym.

Teraz bateria ma 43–83% i tanie ładowanie w sobotę, więc żaden z tych warunków nie zachodzi. Model sam wyłapie takie tygodnie i wtedy zaproponuje dłuższe albo częstsze cykle.

Dokładnych składników 2,40 zł nadal nie widzę, bo plan bez cyklu nie jest zapisywany. Liczba 0,83 zł to moje przybliżenie.

"""Apartment supply: is the apartment fed from the Victron (PPE 1) or meter 2?

A manual switch moves the apartment between the Victron output and the second
point of delivery. Nothing reports its position, so it is told from power
(parent spec ``docs/apartment-supply-planning.plan.md``, 2026-09-14):

* ``a`` = apartment power, ``r`` = Victron output − Σ the other sub-meters
  behind the Victron. Only ``a ≥ P_min`` decides anything: ``meter_2`` when
  ``r < share · a``, else ``victron``. The rule is proportional because the
  apartment meter and the Victron disagree by a few percent at sustained ~2 kW
  loads and report non-simultaneously: an absolute margin (``r ≥ a − 100 W``)
  gave 6-14 false meter-2 episodes in 14 days of real 30 s samples, depending on
  the sampling phase, a share of 0.5 none, while a simulated meter-2 supply was
  still detected.
* N decisive samples of the other state in a row confirm a change; otherwise
  the last confirmed state holds. Before the first confirmation it is unknown.

The pure part (:func:`classify_sample`, :class:`SupplyDetector`,
:func:`hour_supply`, :func:`classify_hours`, :func:`carry_hour_states`,
:func:`past_hour_states`) has no Home Assistant dependency.
:class:`SupplyModule` samples the configured sensors on a fixed tick and keeps
the confirmed transitions in an append-only log in its own store. At setup the
same detector first replays the recorder's state history of the inputs, on the
same grid, from the last stored transition (or from the oldest history) to now.
Hours older than the log are classified from hourly means
(:meth:`SupplyModule.async_hourly_states`) and carried forward through
undecided hours (:func:`carry_hour_states`); :meth:`SupplyModule.async_past_hour_states`
joins them with the log into one state per past hour for the meter tree
(``hierarchy.exclusive_series``). The module adds nothing to the forecast
itself: while it is active the consumption and climate modules forecast the
apartment's subtree (:meth:`SupplyModule.apartment_devices`) apart from the
Victron demand, in every state, and the optimizer places it on the Victron or
on meter 2 per the hour's supply. While the state is unknown the plan carries
a reminder.

"""Backtest the apartment-supply rule on exported hourly statistics.

Checks the rule of ``custom_components/powerpilot/modules/supply.py`` against
the second point of delivery's own import statistic: an hour in which meter 2
imported energy is the ground truth "the apartment was on meter 2".

Usage::

    python3 scripts/backtest_supply_detector.py export.json

Producing ``export.json`` from a Home Assistant instance: call the
``recorder/statistics_during_period`` websocket command (Developer tools
cannot do it; use any websocket client with a long-lived token) once with
``period: "hour"`` and ``types: ["mean"]`` for the apartment power sensor, the
Victron output power sensor and each other sub-meter's power sensor behind the
Victron, and once with ``types: ["change"]`` for the long-term statistic of the
second point of delivery's hourly import (kWh). Align the answers by hour
start and write::

    {"min_apartment_w": 300, "victron_share": 0.5,
     "hours": [{"start": "2026-06-01T10:00:00+02:00",
                "apartment_w": 850.0,      # hourly mean, W (null = no data)
                "victron_w": 1020.0,       # hourly mean of the Victron output, W
                "others_w": [40.0, 15.5],  # hourly means of the other sub-meters, W
                "ppe2_kwh": 0.0},          # meter 2 hourly import, kWh
               ...]}

Power in kW must be converted to W before export. Standard library only: the
script does not import Home Assistant.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Hourly import above this (kWh) counts as "the apartment was on meter 2".
PPE2_TRUTH_KWH = 0.05

VICTRON = "victron"
METER_2 = "meter_2"


def classify_sample(apartment_w, victron_net_w, min_apartment_w, victron_share):
    """Same rule as ``classify_sample`` in ``modules/supply.py`` (keep in sync)."""
    if apartment_w < min_apartment_w:
        return None
    return METER_2 if victron_net_w < victron_share * apartment_w else VICTRON


def backtest(data: dict) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Count the rule's verdicts against the PPE 2 truth for every hour."""
    min_w = float(data["min_apartment_w"])
    victron_share = float(data["victron_share"])
    counts = {
        "true_meter_2": 0,  # truth meter_2, decided meter_2
        "false_victron": 0,  # truth meter_2, decided victron
        "true_victron": 0,  # truth victron, decided victron
        "false_meter_2": 0,  # truth victron, decided meter_2
        "undecided_truth_meter_2": 0,
        "undecided_truth_victron": 0,
        "missing_data": 0,
    }
    for hour in data["hours"]:
        apartment = hour.get("apartment_w")
        victron = hour.get("victron_w")
        others = hour.get("others_w") or []
        ppe2 = hour.get("ppe2_kwh")
        if (
            apartment is None
            or victron is None
            or ppe2 is None
            or not others
            or any(o is None for o in others)
        ):
            counts["missing_data"] += 1
            continue
        truth = METER_2 if ppe2 > PPE2_TRUTH_KWH else VICTRON
        decided = classify_sample(apartment, victron - sum(others), min_w, victron_share)
        if decided is None:
            counts[f"undecided_truth_{truth}"] += 1
        elif truth == METER_2:
            counts["true_meter_2" if decided == METER_2 else "false_victron"] += 1
        else:
            counts["true_victron" if decided == VICTRON else "false_meter_2"] += 1
    return counts


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if len(args) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    counts = backtest(json.loads(Path(args[0]).read_text()))
    total = sum(counts.values())
    print(f"hours: {total}")
    print("                  decided meter_2   decided victron   undecided")
    print(
        f"truth meter_2     {counts['true_meter_2']:>15}   {counts['false_victron']:>15}"
        f"   {counts['undecided_truth_meter_2']:>9}"
    )
    print(
        f"truth victron     {counts['false_meter_2']:>15}   {counts['true_victron']:>15}"
        f"   {counts['undecided_truth_victron']:>9}"
    )
    print(f"missing data: {counts['missing_data']}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

        "undecided_truth_meter_2": 0,
        "undecided_truth_victron": 0,
        "missing_data": 0,
    }
    for hour in data["hours"]:
        apartment = hour.get("apartment_w")
        victron = hour.get("victron_w")
        others = hour.get("others_w") or []
        ppe2 = hour.get("ppe2_kwh")
        if (
            apartment is None
            or victron is None
            or ppe2 is None
            or not others
            or any(o is None for o in others)
        ):
            counts["missing_data"] += 1
            continue
        truth = METER_2 if ppe2 > PPE2_TRUTH_KWH else VICTRON
        decided = classify_sample(apartment, victron - sum(others), min_w, victron_share)
        if decided is None:
            counts[f"undecided_truth_{truth}"] += 1
        elif truth == METER_2:
            counts["true_meter_2" if decided == METER_2 else "false_victron"] += 1
        else:
            counts["true_victron" if decided == VICTRON else "false_meter_2"] += 1
    return counts


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if len(args) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    counts = backtest(json.loads(Path(args[0]).read_text()))
    total = sum(counts.values())
    print(f"hours: {total}")
    print("                  decided meter_2   decided victron   undecided")
    print(
        f"truth meter_2     {counts['true_meter_2']:>15}   {counts['false_victron']:>15}"
        f"   {counts['undecided_truth_meter_2']:>9}"
    )
    print(
        f"truth victron     {counts['false_meter_2']:>15}   {counts['true_victron']:>15}"
        f"   {counts['undecided_truth_victron']:>9}"
    )
    print(f"missing data: {counts['missing_data']}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# --- Apartment supply (which point of delivery feeds the apartment) ---
# A manual switch moves the apartment between the Victron output (PPE 1) and
# the second meter (PPE 2). ``modules/supply.py`` tells which from power alone:
# with the apartment drawing at least ``supply_min_apartment_w``, it is on the
# Victron unless the Victron output minus the other sub-meters behind it covers
# less than ``supply_victron_share`` of the apartment's power (a proportional
# rule: the meters disagree by a few percent, so an absolute margin gave false
# meter-2 episodes); ``supply_confirm_samples`` agreeing
# samples in a row confirm a change. Detection is on only when the apartment
# sensor, the Victron output sensor and the other sub-meters are all set.

# meter subtree moves with the apartment between the two supplies.

CONF_VICTRON_OUTPUT_POWER_SENSOR: Final = "victron_output_power_sensor"  # W or kW
# Power sensors of the other loads behind the Victron (outside the apartment).
CONF_VICTRON_OTHER_POWER_SENSORS: Final = "victron_other_power_sensors"
CONF_SUPPLY_MIN_APARTMENT_W: Final = "supply_min_apartment_w"
CONF_SUPPLY_VICTRON_SHARE: Final = "supply_victron_share"

    async def async_step_supply(self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ConfigFlowResult:
        """Which point of delivery feeds the apartment: inputs and thresholds."""
        self._ensure_loaded()
        meters = [
            selector.SelectOptionDict(value=eid, label=self._friendly(eid))
            for eid in metered_sensors(self._data)
        ]
        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        if user_input is not None:
            errors = _supply_errors(user_input, self._data)
            if not errors:
                for key in (*_SUPPLY_SENSOR_KEYS, CONF_APARTMENT_METER):
                    if user_input.get(key):
                        self._data[key] = user_input[key]
                    else:
                        self._data.pop(key, None)
                others = list(user_input.get(CONF_VICTRON_OTHER_POWER_SENSORS) or [])
                if others:
                    self._data[CONF_VICTRON_OTHER_POWER_SENSORS] = others
                else:
                    self._data.pop(CONF_VICTRON_OTHER_POWER_SENSORS, None)
                self._data[CONF_SUPPLY_MIN_APARTMENT_W] = float(
                    user_input[CONF_SUPPLY_MIN_APARTMENT_W]
                )
                self._data[CONF_SUPPLY_VICTRON_SHARE] = float(
                    user_input[CONF_SUPPLY_VICTRON_SHARE]
                )
                # Replaced by the share (a change of meaning gets a new key).
                self._data.pop(_OBSOLETE_SUPPLY_MARGIN_KEY, None)
                self._data[CONF_SUPPLY_CONFIRM_SAMPLES] = int(
                    user_input[CONF_SUPPLY_CONFIRM_SAMPLES]
                )
                self._data[CONF_SUPPLY_RECOMMENDATIONS] = bool(
                    user_input[CONF_SUPPLY_RECOMMENDATIONS]
                )
                self._data[CONF_SUPPLY_CYCLE_THRESHOLD_PLN] = float(
                    user_input[CONF_SUPPLY_CYCLE_THRESHOLD_PLN]
                )
                for key in (
                    CONF_SUPPLY_MIN_STAY_HOURS,
                    CONF_SUPPLY_QUIET_START_HOUR,
                    CONF_SUPPLY_QUIET_END_HOUR,
                ):
                    self._data[key] = int(user_input[key])

ON_METER_2 = (1000.0, 120.0)
IDLE = (150.0, 0.0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The rule
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_rule_decides_only_above_the_minimum_and_below_the_share() -> None:
    assert classify_sample(299.9, 0.0, 300.0, 0.5) is None
    assert classify_sample(300.0, 150.0, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_VICTRON  # r == share * a
    assert classify_sample(300.0, 149.9, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_METER_2
    assert classify_sample(2000.0, 2500.0, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_VICTRON


def test_rule_is_proportional_not_an_absolute_margin() -> None:
    """Live 2026-10: ``r >= a - 100 W`` gave 6-14 false meter-2 episodes in 14 days.

    The apartment meter and the Victron disagree by a few percent at ~2 kW and
    do not report simultaneously; 1850 W against 2000 W is the Victron.
    """
    assert classify_sample(2000.0, 1850.0, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_VICTRON
    assert classify_sample(2000.0, 900.0, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_METER_2
    # The same 150 W gap at 500 W is a real difference of 30 %, still the Victron.
    assert classify_sample(500.0, 350.0, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_VICTRON


def test_thresholds_are_parameters_not_constants() -> None:
    # 500 W apartment, 350 W net: victron with a share of 0.5, meter_2 with 0.8.
    assert classify_sample(500.0, 350.0, 300.0, 0.5) == SUPPLY_VICTRON
    assert classify_sample(500.0, 350.0, 300.0, 0.8) == SUPPLY_METER_2
    assert classify_sample(500.0, 350.0, 600.0, 0.5) is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The detector
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_first_confirmation_from_unknown_has_no_lower_bound() -> None:
    detector = _detector()
    assert detector.observe(_t(0), *ON_METER_2) is None
    assert detector.observe(_t(1), *ON_METER_2) is None
    assert detector.state is None
    transition = detector.observe(_t(2), 1100.0, 90.0)

    assert transition == SupplyTransition(
        state=SUPPLY_METER_2,
        at=_t(0),
        not_before=None,
        apartment_w=1100.0,
        victron_net_w=90.0,
        source=SUPPLY_SOURCE_LIVE,
    )
    assert detector.state == SUPPLY_METER_2
    assert detector.streak == 0


def test_from_unknown_a_streak_of_the_other_state_starts_over() -> None:
    detector = _detector()
    detector.observe(_t(0), *ON_VICTRON)
    detector.observe(_t(1), *ON_VICTRON)
    assert detector.observe(_t(2), *ON_METER_2) is None
    assert detector.observe(_t(3), *ON_METER_2) is None
    transition = detector.observe(_t(4), *ON_METER_2)
    assert transition is not None
    assert (transition.state, transition.at, transition.not_before) == (
        SUPPLY_METER_2,
        _t(2),
        None,
    )


def test_missing_input_breaks_the_streak() -> None:
    detector = _detector(state=SUPPLY_VICTRON, last_decisive=_t(-1))
    detector.observe(_t(0), *ON_METER_2)
    detector.observe(_t(1), *ON_METER_2)
    assert detector.observe(_t(2), None, 120.0) is None
    assert detector.streak == 0
    detector.observe(_t(3), *ON_METER_2)

## Change 2026-10-17 after the live run

- **Rule is proportional.** The absolute rule `victron when r >= a - 100 W`
  produced 6-14 false "meter 2" episodes (15-23 h) in 14 days of real 30 s
  samples, depending on the sampling phase: the apartment meter and the Victron
  disagree by a few percent at sustained ~2 kW loads and report non-
  simultaneously. The new rule: `meter_2` when `r < share * a`, else `victron`
  (`supply_victron_share`, default 0.5; the key `supply_margin_w` is gone and
  the options step removes it from stored options). It gave zero false episodes
  at every phase and still detected a simulated meter-2 supply.
- **N = 10** (was 3): with it there was also no false return to the Victron.
- **Negative exclusive values are kept.** The unmetered base behind the Victron
  is ~20 W on average (10 kWh over 21 days against 268 kWh), so its hourly value
  scatters around zero with meter noise: 126 of 504 hours came out negative,
  summing to -6 kWh. Dropping them discarded half the learning days and biased
  the base upward; clamping biased it too. `exclusive_series` now keeps them
  as they are and only counts them in `negative`; a missing child reading still
  drops the hour.

content.text:
Przełączenie zostało wykryte i plan z 19:00 je uwzględnia. Wykrycie przyszło jednak dopiero po 54 minutach.

**Stan w HA (19:00):**
- **Przełączenie:** detektor potwierdził licznik 2 o 18:52:36. Wpisał 18:02:05, a fizycznie przełączyłeś o 17:58:50. Te ~3 minuty policzyły się na PPE 1, to około 0,01 kWh.
- **Powiadomienie:** zniknęło, przełączenie nie jest już wymagane.
- **Plan:** mieszkanie jest na liczniku 2 i cykl jest w toku. Powrót na Victrona zaplanowany na 20.10 około 16:00. Pozostanie na liczniku 2 do tej pory model wycenia na około 2,03 zł.
- **PPE 2:** policzone już 0,32 kWh z godziny 18:00. Ta godzina jest jeszcze liczona z danych 5-minutowych, bo HA nie domknęło statystyki godzinowej. Tarcza obejmuje PPE 2, plan rozliczenia to 12,32 zł. Średnia PPE 1 to 0,48 zł/kWh, pod limitem.
- **Czas odświeżania wzrósł:** o 19:00 plan był gotowy po 10,3 s, a encje po 20,7 s. Samo przeliczenie cyklu w toku zajęło 10,4 s. O 18:00 całość trwała 10,5 s, więc z cyklem w toku jest wyraźnie wolniej. Nie wiem jeszcze dlaczego. Obserwuję kolejne godziny, zanim coś zmienię.

**Dlaczego wykrycie trwało tak długo:** detektor rozstrzyga dopiero przy mieszkaniu ≥ 300 W, a mieszkanie pobierało ~240 W. Poprzednią rozstrzygającą próbkę miał o 12:18. Na 14 dniach surowych próbek próg 200 W:
- nie dał żadnego fałszywego alarmu,
- wykryłby dzisiejsze przełączenie po ~4,5 min.

Próg 120 W dał już fałszywy alarm.

**W repo:** commit `920755f` zmienia domyślny próg na 200 W. Dodałem dwa testy oparte na dzisiejszych pomiarach: pierwszy przy 300 W nie przechodzi, drugi przy 120 W nie przechodzi. Uzupełniłem też README i plan etapu 2. Cały zestaw przeszedł: 619/619. Nie pushowałem. Twoje HA ma 300 W zapisane w opcjach, więc i tak trzeba je zmienić ręcznie.

**Zmiany w HA nie zapisałem.** Tryb uprawnień zablokował mi zapis opcji integracji, mimo Twojej zgody. Formularz otworzyłem, ale niczego nie zapisałem. Ustaw to sam:

1. Ustawienia → Urządzenia oraz usługi → PowerPilot → Konfiguruj.
2. Wybierz „🏠 Zasilanie mieszkania”.
3. W polu „Minimalna moc mieszkania do rozstrzygnięcia” wpisz 200 i zatwierdź.
4. Wybierz „✅ Zapisz i zakończ”.

Integracja się przeładuje. Log przejść odbuduje się z historii i powinien przestawić datę przełączenia na około 17:59.

Ten sam formularz pokazuje „Próg opłacalności cyklu” 1 zł, a nie ustalone wcześniej 2 zł. Zmieniono go przy zapisie opcji o 17:43, nie ja. Jeśli tak miało być, zostaw.

    def current_decision(
        self, plan: Plan | None = None, moment: datetime | None = None
    ) -> Decision | None:
        """Decision covering the current clock hour in the latest plan."""
        active_plan = self.data if plan is None else plan
        if active_plan is None:
            return None
        return active_plan.decision_at(moment or dt_util.now())

    async def async_setup_modules(self) -> None:
        await self.registry.async_setup_all()
        await self._async_setup_snapshots()
        # A confirmed switch ends (or starts) a required switch between plans.
        self.entry.async_on_unload(
            async_dispatcher_connect(
                self.hass, self.supply.signal, self._async_on_supply_changed
            )
        )

    @callback
    def _async_on_supply_changed(self) -> None:
        self._sync_switch_notification(self.data)

    async def _async_setup_snapshots(self) -> None:
        self._snapshot_store = Store(
            self.hass,
            STORAGE_VERSION_SNAPSHOTS,
            f"{DOMAIN}_{self.entry.entry_id}_snapshots",
        )
        stored = await self._snapshot_store.async_load()
        self.snapshots = SnapshotStore.from_dict(stored)
        self.snapshots.prune()
        # Restore the modelled battery energy cost (no sensor exists for it, so a
        # restart would otherwise reset it to 0 and wipe the cost basis of energy
        # already stored — making "Cena w baterii" drop to ~0 until it rebuilds).
        if stored:
            self._battery_energy_cost = float(stored.get("battery_energy_cost") or 0.0)
            # Restore the once-per-hour snapshot guard so a mid-hour restart
            # leaves the already-recorded vintage untouched.
            self._last_snapshot_hour = (
                dt_util.parse_datetime(stored.get("last_snapshot_hour") or "")
                or None
            )
            self.switch_notices = SwitchNotices.from_list(stored.get("supply_notified"))

    def _snapshots_payload(self) -> dict:
        return {
            **self.snapshots.to_dict(),
            "battery_energy_cost": round(self._battery_energy_cost, 6),
            # Persisted so a restart within the same hour doesn't re-record the
            # active hour's vintage (which would overwrite the charging plan with
            # a restart-time re-plan and corrupt the forecast statistics).
            "last_snapshot_hour": (
                self._last_snapshot_hour.isoformat()
                if self._last_snapshot_hour
                else None
            ),
            # Switch notifications already shown: never repeated after a restart.
            "supply_notified": self.switch_notices.to_list(),
                f"Odtworzono historię zasilania mieszkania: {len(appended)} "
                f"przejść, {samples} próbek, w tym {missing} bez kompletu odczytów.",
                extra={
                    "from": start.isoformat() if start is not None else None,
                    "transitions": len(appended),
                    "samples": samples,
                    "missing_samples": missing,
                },
            )
            detector.source = SUPPLY_SOURCE_LIVE
        self.detector = detector
        entry = self.coordinator.entry
        entry.async_on_unload(
            async_track_time_interval(
                self.hass, self._async_tick, SUPPLY_SAMPLE_INTERVAL
            )
        )
        # Home Assistant does not unload entries when it stops: both save.
        entry.async_on_unload(self._async_save_checkpoint_now)
        entry.async_on_unload(
            self.hass.bus.async_listen_once(EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP, self._async_on_stop)
        )
        async_dispatcher_send(self.hass, self.signal)

    async def _async_move_store_aside(self, err: ValueError) -> None:
        """Keep an undecodable log for inspection and refuse to save over it.

        Home Assistant's ``Store`` itself moves a file that is not valid JSON
        aside; this covers valid JSON this module cannot decode. The module
        stays inert for this run — no sampling, no save — so the bad file is
        never replaced by an empty log.
        at = dt_util.as_utc(now)
        if self.covered_from is None:
            # Nothing was replayed: the log watches from its first live sample.
            self.covered_from = at
        streak_before = self.detector.streak
        apartment_w, victron_net_w = self._sample()
        transition = self.detector.observe(at, apartment_w, victron_net_w)
        self._last_tick_at = at
        if transition is not None:
            self.transitions.append(transition)
        # Never mid-streak: resuming from the checkpoint must lose no partial streak.
        checkpoint_due = self.detector.streak == 0 and (
            transition is not None
            or self.checkpoint is None
            or at - self.checkpoint.at >= SUPPLY_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL
        )
        if checkpoint_due:
            self.checkpoint = SupplyCheckpoint(at, self.detector.last_decisive)
        if transition is not None or checkpoint_due:
            await self._async_save()
        if transition is not None:
            self.log_info(
                f"Zasilanie mieszkania: {transition.state} od {transition.at.isoformat()}",
                extra=transition.to_dict(),
            )
        if transition is not None or self.detector.streak != streak_before:
            async_dispatcher_send(self.hass, self.signal)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # History
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

"""Refresh the plan when calendars, presence or the EV plug change.

        The hourly cadence stays the baseline; this listener closes the gap
        between "the world changed" and the next boundary: an event added to
        the calendar, the car driving off or getting plugged back in. Calendar
        entities fire on any change (their next-event attributes matter);
        presence/plug/charging entities only on an actual state flip, so GPS
        attribute chatter from phone trackers doesn't re-run the optimizer
        every few minutes. ``async_request_refresh`` debounces bursts. The ESS
        SoC sensor re-plans only when it crosses the reserve-recovery latch
        (below the minimum / back above the margin), so a drained pack is
        charged back at once instead of at the next clock hour.
        """
        soc_id = str(self.config.get(CONF_SOC_SENSOR) or "")
        calendar_ids = [str(e) for e in (self.config.get(CONF_CALENDARS) or [])]
        flip_ids = [
            str(e)
            for e in (
                [
                    self.config.get(CONF_EV_LOCATION_SENSOR),
                    self.config.get(CONF_EV_PLUG_SENSOR),
                    self.config.get(CONF_EV_CHARGING_SENSOR),
                ]
                + list(self.config.get(CONF_EV_PRESENCE_ENTITIES) or [])
            )
            if e
        ]
        entities = calendar_ids + flip_ids + ([soc_id] if soc_id else [])
        if not entities:
            return None
        presence_set = set(flip_ids)

        # Entity → role, so a recorded re-plan can name what caused it.
        roles: dict[str, str] = {eid: "calendar" for eid in calendar_ids}
        for conf_key, role in _TRIGGER_ROLE_KEYS.items():
            entity_id = self.config.get(conf_key)
            if entity_id:
                roles[str(entity_id)] = role
        for entity_id in self.config.get(CONF_EV_PRESENCE_ENTITIES) or []:
            roles.setdefault(str(entity_id), "presence")
        if soc_id:
            roles[soc_id] = "reserve"
        self._trigger_roles = roles

        @callback
        def _on_state_change(event) -> None:
            entity_id = event.data.get("entity_id")
            old = event.data.get("old_state")
            new = event.data.get("new_state")
            if new is None:
                return
            if entity_id in presence_set and old is not None and old.state == new.state:
                return
            if entity_id == soc_id and not self._soc_flips_recovery(new.state):
                return
            self._note_trigger(entity_id, new)
            self.hass.async_create_task(self.async_request_refresh())

        return async_track_state_change_event(self.hass, entities, _on_state_change)

    @callback
    def _note_trigger(self, entity_id: str | None, new_state) -> None:
        """Remember what caused the upcoming re-plan, in the panel's language.

        Labels dedupe by role, so a burst across several presence entities reads
        as one "obecność" and the list stays bounded by the number of roles.
    for bad in ({"x": 1}, [["x", SUPPLY_METER_2]], [{"id": "x", "direction": "up"}]):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            SwitchNotices.from_list(bad)

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.saves: list[float] = []

    def async_delay_save(self, _payload, delay: float) -> None:
        self.saves.append(delay)


def _fake_coordinator(plan, planning, state: dict, notices: SwitchNotices):
    fake = SimpleNamespace(

# Why a mid-hour re-plan ran, in the panel's language. The reactive listener
# knows which entity flipped; without that label a recorded revision only says
# "the plan changed", not "because the cable went in" — which is the whole point
# of recording it. Role → (config key it comes from) and the words for the flip.
_TRIGGER_ROLE_KEYS: Final[dict[str, str]] = {
    CONF_EV_PLUG_SENSOR: "plug",
    CONF_EV_CHARGING_SENSOR: "charging",
    CONF_EV_LOCATION_SENSOR: "location",
}
_TRIGGER_LABELS: Final[dict[str, str]] = {
    "plug": "kabel EV",
    "charging": "ładowanie EV",
    "location": "lokalizacja auta",
    "presence": "obecność",
    "calendar": "kalendarz",
    "reserve": "rezerwa ESS",
}
# Role → (states that read as "yes", word for yes, word for no). Mirrors the EV
# module's own dialect sets, so the label matches what the planner concluded.
_TRIGGER_STATES: Final[dict[str, tuple[set[str], str, str]]] = {
    "plug": (PLUGGED_STATES, "podłączono", "odłączono"),
    "charging": (CHARGING_STATES, "start", "stop"),
    "location": (HOME_STATES, "w domu", "poza domem"),
    "presence": (HOME_STATES, "w domu", "poza domem"),
}
_UNKNOWN_STATES: Final = ("unknown", "unavailable", "none", "")

# A re-plan counts as a revision only past these thresholds (see
# ``_plan_row_differs``): 0.1 kW of charge power, 0.05 kWh of EV energy.
_REVISION_POWER_EPS: Final = 0.1
_REVISION_EV_EPS: Final = 0.05
# How long a charger may overrun the end of a planned hour before the spill into
# the next hour stops reading as "that session finishing" (see ``_ev_off_plan``).
_EV_SPILL_MINUTES: Final = 10


class PowerPilotCoordinator(DataUpdateCoordinator[Plan]):

        self.entry = entry
        self.config: dict = {**DEFAULTS, **entry.data, **entry.options}
        self._battery_energy_cost = 0.0
        # Reserve-recovery latch (battery.next_recovery_state): on once the live
        # SoC fell below the minimum, off once it is back above the margin.
        self._ess_recovering = False
        # Plan execution watchdog (execution.py): how long the planned mode has
        # held, and the alarm the binary sensor mirrors (on: None = cannot say).
        self._execution_watch = ExecutionWatch()
        self.execution_alarm: dict = {"on": None, "reason": None, "mode": None, "since": None}
        self.events: deque = deque(maxlen=50)
        # What triggered the re-plan currently being computed (entity flips seen
        # by the reactive listener), and the entity → role map that names them.
        # Consumed by the snapshot recorder, which labels each mid-hour revision
        # with its cause.
        self._pending_triggers: list[str] = []
        self._trigger_roles: dict[str, str] = {}
        # Last reason each PPE's monthly price cap could not be modelled, and
        # why apartment switches were not planned — logged once per distinct
        # reason instead of on every refresh.
        self._billing_unavailable_logged: dict[str, str] = {}

# Web frontends and PWAs

- iOS clears `sessionStorage` for home-screen PWAs; keep auth tokens in `localStorage`, with a
  one-time read of the old key when migrating.
- Bump the service worker cache version whenever static files change.
- Mobile layout: inputs at least 16px font (iOS zooms otherwise) and no horizontal overflow; guard
  both with a test when the app is used on phones.
- Enforce policy on the server; never trust a setting the client sends.
- Check real rendered output (`getComputedStyle`, the actual output of third-party editors) rather
  than a screenshot impression or hand-written expectations.

async def _observe(
        self,
        ppe: str,
        hours: "_PpeHours",
        now: datetime,
        terms: PriceCapTerms,
        archive: SplitArchive | None = None,
    ) -> BillingPeriod:
        """Read the month-to-date import + cap cost of one PPE under ``terms``.

        ``hours`` says what each hour of the PPE is made of; the rules for
        expected, covered, missing and pending hours, the cap price and the
        recorder's latency are the same for every PPE and live here.
        ``archive`` keeps the 5-minute reads of completed hours (PPE 2's
        splits) past the short-term statistics' retention.
        """
        month_start, month_end = month_bounds(now)
        hour_now = now.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)

        # Completed hours: hourly statistics. The reader drops the first row of
        # a window (it needs a predecessor to difference), hence the lead-in.
        series: dict[str, dict[datetime, float]] = {}
        for entity_id in hours.meters:
            series[entity_id] = await self._meters.async_range_kwh(
                entity_id, month_start - _HOUR, hour_now
            )

        energy = 0.0
        cost = 0.0
        expected = 0
        covered = 0
        missing: list[str] = []
        pending: list[str] = []
        gaps = 0

        def note(reason: str) -> None:
            nonlocal gaps
            gaps += 1
            if len(missing) < _MAX_MISSING_LISTED:
                missing.append(reason)

        async def account(
            label: str, hour: datetime, read: _HourRead, completed: bool
        ) -> None:
            nonlocal energy, cost, covered
            if read.gap is not None:
                note(f"{label}: {read.gap}")
                return
            values: list[float] = []
            absent: list[str] = []
            from_buckets = False
            for eid in read.hourly:
                value = series[eid].get(hour)
                if value is None and now - (hour + _HOUR) <= _RECORDER_LATENCY:
                    # The hourly statistic of an hour that just ended is still
                    # on its way: read the hour from its 5-minute buckets. An
                    # hour without a single bucket is a real hole in the
                    # recorder.
                    value = await self._meters.async_partial_kwh(eid, hour, hour + _HOUR)
                    from_buckets = from_buckets or value is not None
                if value is None:
                    absent.append(eid)
                else:
                    values.append(value)
            waiting: list[datetime] = []
            archivable = (
                archive is not None

async def test_series_without_detection_carries_no_supply(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
    await _setup(hass)
    coordinator = hass.data[DOMAIN][next(iter(hass.data[DOMAIN]))]
    result = await coordinator.get_series(past_hours=2)
    past = [h for h in result["hours"] if h["is_past"] and not h.get("partial")]
    future = [h for h in result["hours"] if not h["is_past"]]
    assert past and future
    assert all(h["supply_actual"] is None for h in past)
    assert all(h["supply_planned"] is None for h in future)

    forecast, battery, billing, planning = _weak()
    plan = _optimizer().optimize(forecast, battery, billing=billing, supply=planning)

    assert plan.supply_switching is True
    assert _on_meter_2(plan) == [0, 1, 1]

        SUPPLY_METER_2,
        SUPPLY_METER_2,
    ]
    # On meter 2 the battery covers only the Victron's own demand (the product
    # z·s takes the apartment's share off the discharge).
    assert [round(d.battery_discharge_kwh, 6) for d in plan.decisions] == [0.0, 1.0, 1.0]
    assert [round(d.grid_buy_kwh, 6) for d in plan.decisions] == [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

Wykres poprawiłem w kodzie (dwa lokalne commity, 622/622 testów), ale w HA jeszcze go nie widać, bo nie robiłem pusha ani instalacji. Cykl na cały tydzień to nie awaria.

**Dlaczego cały tydzień na liczniku 2.** W ten weekend licznik 2 i bateria idą łeb w łeb.
- Od niedzieli do wtorku nie ma tanich godzin: najtańsza energia z dystrybucją kosztuje 0,89–0,91 zł, a w sobotę było 0,71 zł.
- Bateria nawet bez mieszkania schodzi według planu do minimum 6% i doładowuje się dopiero w środę.
- Mieszkanie na PPE 2 przez tydzień to 41,95 zł za ~51 kWh. Idealny PPE 1, czyli bateria bez limitów ładowana zawsze w najtańszej godzinie, wyszedłby 38,84 zł.
- Model z prawdziwymi limitami pojemności i mocy ładowania daje PPE 2 przewagę około 2,8 zł.

Brak powrotu w planie znaczy „w tym tygodniu nie przełączaj z powrotem”. Gdy pojawią się tanie godziny, plan zaproponuje powrót i dostaniesz powiadomienie. Wcześniejszy powrót 20.10 zniknął, bo przyszły nowe prognozy cen, a różnica była rzędu złotówek.

**Wykres był faktycznie zepsuty.**
- **Przyczyna:** w godzinach na liczniku 2 serwer wyrzucał prognozę mieszkania i całego jego poddrzewa. Tak było zaprojektowane, żeby słupki urządzeń zgadzały się z zużyciem Victrona. Przy tygodniu na liczniku 2 mieszkanie zniknęło z wykresu w całości.
- **Przeszłe godziny:** odczyty mieszkania było widać, ale zużycie nie bilansowało się z zasilaniem.
- **Po poprawce:** zużycie pokazuje wszystkie urządzenia, łącznie z mieszkaniem. Strona zasilania ma „⚡ Import z sieci — PPE 1”, „⚡ Import z sieci — PPE 2” (jaśniejszy fiolet) i rozładowanie ESS. Dymek pokazuje oba importy.
- **Bilans:** słupki w górę i w dół znów się zgadzają. Godzina z przełączeniem w środku nie ma jeszcze importu PPE 2 ani bazy, bo jej podziału nie odczytam z godzinowych liczników. To uczciwy brak, nie zgadywana liczba.

Commity to `4e4a27d` (dane serii) i `695f4e3` (panel). README też poprawiłem.

**Nadal pokazują tylko PPE 1:**
- wykres kosztów pod spodem: słupki „Koszt energii — sieć” nie zawierają kosztu mieszkania na PPE 2,
- karta „Sterowanie — realizacja vs plan” w wierszu „Pobór z sieci”,
- zakładka „Przepływ”.

Poprawię je, jeśli chcesz.

    """Meter 2's hour on the cost chart costs what its month settles at.

    While PPE 2's month binds every kWh costs the limit, however expensive
    the hour; while it does not, or on a day no Tarcza covers, the hour's
    energy price as on PPE 1. Distribution is the hour's either way. A month
    whose settlement is unknown has no cost rather than the market one.
    """
    from datetime import timedelta
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    from custom_components.powerpilot.const import PPE_1, PPE_2
    from custom_components.powerpilot.coordinator import PowerPilotCoordinator
    from custom_components.powerpilot.models import BillingOutcome
    from tests.test_optimizer_supply import H0, LIMIT, _period

    def outcome(ppe: str, binds: bool | None) -> BillingOutcome:
        return BillingOutcome(
            period=_period(ppe, 10.0, 20.0),
            energy_kwh=10.0,
            cost_pln=20.0,
            cap_binds=binds,
            settled_cost_pln=10.0 * LIMIT if binds else 20.0,
            planned_energy_kwh=0.0,
            tail_energy_kwh=0.0,
        )

    def cost(binds, *, tarcza=True, kwh=2.0, hour=H0):
        stub = SimpleNamespace(
            billing=SimpleNamespace(terms_on=lambda day: object() if tarcza else None),
            data=SimpleNamespace(billing=[outcome(PPE_1, False), outcome(PPE_2, binds)]),
        )
        return PowerPilotCoordinator._ppe2_hour_cost(stub, hour, kwh, 1.8, 0.5)

    assert cost(True) == round(2.0 * (LIMIT + 0.5), 4)
    assert cost(False) == round(2.0 * (1.8 + 0.5), 4)
    assert cost(None, tarcza=False) == round(2.0 * (1.8 + 0.5), 4)
    assert cost(None) is None  # the month could not be modelled
    assert cost(True, hour=H0 + timedelta(days=90)) is None  # no outcome for it
    assert cost(True, kwh=0.0) == 0.0
    assert cost(True, kwh=None) is None


'''

    whose settlement is unknown has no cost rather than the market one.
    """
    from datetime import timedelta
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    from custom_components.powerpilot.const import PPE_1, PPE_2
    from custom_components.powerpilot.coordinator import PowerPilotCoordinator
    from custom_components.powerpilot.models import BillingOutcome
    from tests.test_optimizer_supply import H0, LIMIT, _period

    def outcome(ppe: str, binds: bool | None) -> BillingOutcome:
        return BillingOutcome(
            period=_period(ppe, 10.0, 20.0),
            energy_kwh=10.0,
            cost_pln=20.0,
            cap_binds=binds,
            settled_cost_pln=10.0 * LIMIT if binds else 20.0,
            planned_energy_kwh=0.0,
            tail_energy_kwh=0.0,
        )

    def cost(binds, *, tarcza=True, kwh=2.0, hour=H0):
        stub = SimpleNamespace(
            billing=SimpleNamespace(terms_on=lambda day: object() if tarcza else None),
            data=SimpleNamespace(billing=[outcome(PPE_1, False), outcome(PPE_2, binds)]),
        )
        return PowerPilotCoordinator._ppe2_hour_cost(stub, hour, kwh, 1.8, 0.5)

    assert cost(True) == round(2.0 * (LIMIT + 0.5), 4)
    assert cost(False) == round(2.0 * (1.8 + 0.5), 4)
    assert cost(None, tarcza=False) == round(2.0 * (1.8 + 0.5), 4)
    assert cost(None) is None  # the month could not be modelled
    assert cost(True, hour=H0 + timedelta(days=90)) is None  # no outcome for it
    assert cost(True, kwh=0.0) == 0.0
    assert cost(True, kwh=None) is None


'''

import pathlib
P = pathlib.Path('custom_components/powerpilot/modules/supply.py'); s = P.read_text()
old = '''    def _sample(self) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
        apartment_w = self._read_watts(self.apartment_sensor)
        victron_w = self._read_watts(self.victron_sensor)
        others = [self._read_watts(e) for e in self.other_sensors]
        return apartment_w, victron_net(victron_w, others)
'''
new = '''    def live_reading(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The detection's inputs now, as the next tick reads them (W).

        ``apartment_w`` is ``a``; ``victron_net_w`` is ``r`` = the Victron's
        output minus every other sub-meter behind it (``others_w`` by entity).
        """
        apartment_w = self._read_watts(self.apartment_sensor)
        victron_w = self._read_watts(self.victron_sensor)
        others = {e: self._read_watts(e) for e in self.other_sensors}
        return {
            "apartment_w": apartment_w,
            "victron_w": victron_w,
            "others_w": others,
            "victron_net_w": victron_net(victron_w, list(others.values())),
        }

    def _sample(self) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
        reading = self.live_reading()
        return reading["apartment_w"], reading["victron_net_w"]
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
P.write_text(s.replace(old, new))
EOF

import pathlib
P = pathlib.Path('custom_components/powerpilot/coordinator.py'); s = P.read_text()

        """The installation as the "Przepływ" diagram draws it.

        What is behind what — PPE 1 and its meters (the EV charger before the
        house meters or behind them, the Victron's AC input), the battery, the
        Victron's AC output with the meter tree under it, the apartment's
        switch between the Victron and PPE 2 — what every sensor reads, and
        how each computed value comes out of them, with the very terms the
        integration uses: the meter tree's own energy (``exclusive_series``),
        PPE 1's import (its meters' sum), PPE 2's (``_ppe2_measured_kwh``) and
        the detection's rule (``SupplyModule.live_reading``).

        Two clocks: power sensors read now (W); energy meters and every
        subtraction show the last complete hour (kWh), whose arithmetic can be
        checked. A value that cannot be read is ``None`` and drawn as missing.
        """
        from .const import (
            CONF_CONSUMPTION_SENSOR,
            CONF_EV_BEHIND_METER,
            CONF_EV_ENERGY_ADDED_SENSOR,
            CONF_GRID_IMPORT_SENSOR,
            CONF_SENSOR_PARENTS,
            CONF_SOC_SENSOR,
            CONF_SUPPLY_CONFIRM_SAMPLES,
            CONF_SUPPLY_MIN_APARTMENT_W,
            CONF_SUPPLY_VICTRON_SHARE,
            CONF_BATTERY_CHARGE_SENSOR,
            CONF_BATTERY_DISCHARGE_SENSOR,
        )
        from .hierarchy import build_children, exclusive_series, metered_sensors
        from .modules.supply import classify_sample

        hour = dt_util.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) - timedelta(hours=1)

        def name(eid: str) -> str:
            state = self.hass.states.get(eid)
            return state.name if state is not None else eid

        def live(eid: str | None) -> dict | None:
            """A sensor's state now, with its unit."""
            if not eid:
                return None
            state = self.hass.states.get(eid)
            usable = state is not None and state.state not in ("unknown", "unavailable")
            return {
                "entity_id": eid,
                "name": name(eid),
                "value": state.state if usable else None,
                "unit": state.attributes.get("unit_of_measurement") if state else None,
            }

        async def hour_kwh(eid: str | None) -> float | None:
            """The meter's energy in ``hour`` (the reader needs the hour before)."""
            if not eid:
                return None
            series = await self.consumption.async_range_kwh(
                eid, hour - timedelta(hours=1), hour + timedelta(hours=1)
            )
            value = series.get(hour)
            return round(value, 3) if value is not None else None

        def outcome(ppe: str) -> dict | None:
            for o in self.data.billing if self.data else []:
                if o.period.ppe == ppe and o.period.month_start <= hour < o.period.month_end:
                    return {
                        "binds": o.cap_binds,
                        "average_kwh": (
                            round(o.average_kwh, 4) if o.average_kwh is not None else None
                        ),
                        "limit_kwh": o.period.limit_kwh,
                        "terms_name": o.period.terms_name,
                    }
            return None

        supply = self.supply
        main = self.config.get(CONF_CONSUMPTION_SENSOR)
        device_ids = metered_sensors(self.config)
        parents = self.config.get(CONF_SENSOR_PARENTS) or {}
        hour_state = (
            (await supply.async_past_hour_states(hour, hour + timedelta(hours=1))).get(hour)
            if supply.active
            else None
        )

        # The meter tree: every meter's reading in the hour and its own energy
        # (the reading minus its direct children; the apartment's subtree is
        # not part of the root's while it is on meter 2).
        tree: dict | None = None
        own: dict[str, float | None] = {}
        if main:
            raw = {eid: await hour_kwh(eid) for eid in [main, *device_ids]}
            exclusive = exclusive_series(
                main,
                device_ids,
                parents,
                {eid: ({hour: v} if v is not None else {}) for eid, v in raw.items()},
                apartment=supply.apartment_meter or None,
                supply={hour: hour_state} if hour_state else None,
            ).series
            own = {
                eid: (round(v, 3) if (v := exclusive.get(eid, {}).get(hour)) is not None else None)
                for eid in raw
            }
            children = build_children(main, device_ids, parents)
            apartment = supply.apartment_meter if supply.active else None
            off_victron = self._off_victron_devices(hour_state)

            def node(eid: str) -> dict:
                return {
                    "entity_id": eid,
                    "name": name(eid),
                    "kwh": raw.get(eid),
                    "own_kwh": own.get(eid),
                    # Index in the chart's device list: the same colour there.
                    "device_index": device_ids.index(eid) if eid in device_ids else None,
                    "apartment": eid == apartment,
                    "climate": self.climate.handles(eid),
                    # Not part of the root's reading this hour (on meter 2).
                    "off_victron": eid in off_victron,
                    "children": [node(c) for c in children.get(eid, [])],
                }

            tree = node(main)
            tree["power"] = live(main)

        ppe1_meters = self.billing.ppe_sensors().get(PPE_1) or []
        ppe1_terms = [
            {"entity_id": eid, "name": name(eid), "kwh": await hour_kwh(eid)}
            for eid in ppe1_meters
        ]
        ppe1_import = (
            round(sum(t["kwh"] for t in ppe1_terms), 3)
            if ppe1_terms and all(t["kwh"] is not None for t in ppe1_terms)
            else None
        )

        detection: dict | None = None
        if supply.active:
            reading = supply.live_reading()
            a, r = reading["apartment_w"], reading["victron_net_w"]
            min_w = float(self.config[CONF_SUPPLY_MIN_APARTMENT_W])
            share = float(self.config[CONF_SUPPLY_VICTRON_SHARE])
            detection = {
                "apartment": live(supply.apartment_sensor),
                "victron_output": live(supply.victron_sensor),
                "others": [live(e) for e in supply.other_sensors],
                "apartment_w": a,
                "victron_w": reading["victron_w"],
                "others_w": reading["others_w"],
                "victron_net_w": r,
                "min_apartment_w": min_w,
                "victron_share": share,
                "confirm_samples": int(self.config[CONF_SUPPLY_CONFIRM_SAMPLES]),
                "decision": (
                    classify_sample(a, r, min_w, share)
                    if a is not None and r is not None
                    else None
                ),
                "streak": supply.detector.streak if supply.detector is not None else None,
            }

        eta_d = float(self.config.get(CONF_DISCHARGE_EFFICIENCY, DEFAULTS[CONF_DISCHARGE_EFFICIENCY]))
        wear = float(self.config.get(CONF_BATTERY_WEAR_COST, DEFAULTS[CONF_BATTERY_WEAR_COST]))
        return {
            "hour": hour.isoformat(),
            "supply": {
                "active": supply.active,
                "state": supply.state,
                "since": supply.since.isoformat() if supply.since else None,
                "hour_state": hour_state,
            },
            "ppe1": {
                "terms": ppe1_terms,
                "import_kwh": ppe1_import,
                "tarcza": outcome(PPE_1),
            },
            "ppe2": (
                {
                    "meter": supply.apartment_meter,
                    "import_kwh": self._ppe2_measured_kwh(hour_state, own),
                    "tarcza": outcome(PPE_2),
                }
                if supply.active
                else None
            ),
            "grid_power": live(self.config.get(CONF_GRID_IMPORT_SENSOR)),
            "ev": (
                {
                    # Off: the charger taps in before the house meters, on PPE 1.
                    "behind_meter": bool(self.config.get(CONF_EV_BEHIND_METER, True)),
                    "soc": self.ev.soc,
                    "plug": live(self.config.get(CONF_EV_PLUG_SENSOR)),
                    "energy_added": live(self.config.get(CONF_EV_ENERGY_ADDED_SENSOR)),
                    "energy_added_kwh": await hour_kwh(
                        self.config.get(CONF_EV_ENERGY_ADDED_SENSOR)
                    ),
                }
                if self.ev.enabled
                else None
            ),
            "battery": {
                "soc": live(self.config.get(CONF_SOC_SENSOR)),
                "charge": live(self.config.get(CONF_BATTERY_CHARGE_SENSOR)),
                "discharge": live(self.config.get(CONF_BATTERY_DISCHARGE_SENSOR)),
                "charge_kwh": await hour_kwh(self.config.get(CONF_BATTERY_CHARGE_SENSOR)),
                "discharge_kwh": await hour_kwh(
                    self.config.get(CONF_BATTERY_DISCHARGE_SENSOR)
                ),
                "delivered_cost": (
                    round(self._battery_energy_cost / eta_d + wear, 4) if eta_d > 0 else None
                ),
            },
            "tree": tree,
            "detection": detection,
        }

'''
